primitives.name: Compact Invariant Coset Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: If E is any Baire set in X, then there exists a compact, invariant subgroup Y of X such that E is a union of cosets of Y, and such that the quotient group X/Y is separable.
primitives.latex: E = \bigcup_{x \in S} xY, \quad X/Y \text{ is separable}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: E: Baire measurable set (dimensionless), X: Topological group (state space), Y: Compact invariant subgroup (symmetry kernel), S: Index set of cosets.
primitives.assumptions: X is a locally compact Hausdorff topological group; E is a Baire set within X.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if X lacks local compactness or if the measure does not admit a compatible Haar structure, leading to non-separable quotients.

layer2.mapping: Maps the extraction of invariant tactical features in sports directly to finding the compact subgroup Y that generates the observed event E.

primitives.name: Measure Completion Regularization
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is sufficient to prove that if U is any bounded open set, then there exists a Baire set E contained in U such that U — E may be covered by a Baire set of measure zero.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: U: Bounded open set (phase volume), E: Inner approximating Baire set, μ: Haar measure (probability mass).
primitives.assumptions: Existence of a left-invariant Haar measure μ on the topological group X.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down for unbounded sets where total Haar measure diverges, preventing probabilistic normalization.

The proof leverages Theorem E to secure the existence of Y, and Theorem F to guarantee the separability of the resulting quotient space via the intersection of open sets. Subsequently, Theorem H utilizes this decomposition to prove the completion regularity of Haar measures. By selecting a maximal Baire subset E within a bounded open set U, the residual difference U - E is shown to be negligible (measure zero). The dualities lie in the tension between the continuous open coverings and the discrete, separable nature of the quotient projections. Failure modes emerge when the underlying group lacks local compactness, causing the quotient to become non-separable and the measure regularization to collapse due to unbounded divergence.
